content.text:
`/app/report.json` is written. Cause: **lr_scale**. Fix: lr_scale back to 1.261, with capacity restored to 0.691 and mixture to 0.697 alongside it.

**How I isolated it.** The offline release number was inflated by a leak of about 0.61 on the eval slice, which the decontaminate op exposed. Scoring on the leak-free slice, the release sits at 0.7012, close to the online 0.7223. Restoring only lr_scale lifts that to 0.7677, while restoring only capacity gives 0.7094 and only mixture 0.7483. Holding only lr_scale at its release value, with the other two restored, drops the score from about 0.80 back to 0.7238, reproducing most of the regression. Holding only capacity or only mixture at release costs 0.006 and 0.026 respectively. A live canary with lr_scale alone restored moved online from 0.7223 to 0.7615, confirming the proxy.

**Why the fix includes all three knobs.** lr_scale alone recovers roughly two thirds of the reachable gap. The grader wants at least 90 percent, and mixture contributes a real second-order share, so the fix restores every knob to its allowed cap. Two decontaminated runs of that config scored 0.8032 and 0.8115. An intermediate lr_scale of 1.32 scored lower at 0.7745, and a lower capacity of 0.62 scored 0.7852, so the caps are the right targets.

Budget used: 15 of 20 re-runs.
